benjamin-territory_1293.name: Benjamin
benjamin-territory_1293.what: The tribal territory allotted to Benjamin, a narrow strip of hill country between Judah and Ephraim.
benjamin-territory_1293.today: The central hills north of Jerusalem, mostly in the West Bank.
key: After the land was surveyed from Shiloh, Benjamin's lot came up between Judah and the sons of Joseph (Joshua 18).
Its boundaries ran from the Jordan near Jericho westward past Bethel and Kiriath-jearim (Joshua 18).
Its towns included Jericho, Bethel, Gibeon, Ramah, and Jebus, which is Jerusalem (Joshua 18).

east-manasseh-half-tribe_1290.name: East Manasseh
east-manasseh-half-tribe_1290.what: The territory east of the Jordan given to half the tribe of Manasseh, covering northern Gilead and Bashan.
east-manasseh-half-tribe_1290.today: Northern Jordan and southern Syria, including the Golan Heights area.
key: Moses gave Gilead and the former kingdom of Og to the half-tribe of Manasseh (Numbers 32).
Jair son of Manasseh took the region of Argob and named its villages after himself (Deuteronomy 3).
Moses' allotment to the half-tribe stretched from Mahanaim through all Bashan (Joshua 13).
Because of their unfaithfulness, the Assyrian king Tiglath-pileser carried the half-tribe into exile (1 Chronicles 5).
Manasseh receives a portion in Ezekiel's vision of the restored land (Ezekiel 48).

elam_365.name: Elam
elam_365.what: An ancient nation east of Babylonia whose capital region included Susa.
elam_365.today: Southwestern Iran, around the modern province of Khuzestan.
key: Chedorlaomer king of Elam led a coalition of kings that captured Lot (Genesis 14).
Isaiah foresaw the Lord recovering a remnant of his people from Elam (Isaiah 11).
Elam and Media are summoned to besiege Babylon (Isaiah 21).
Jeremiah announced judgment on Elam but promised to restore its fortunes in the latter days (Jeremiah 49).
Daniel saw his vision of the ram and goat while at Susa in the province of Elam (Daniel 8).

geba_447.name: Geba
geba_447.what: A Levitical town in Benjamin north of Jerusalem, often marking the northern edge of Judah.
geba_447.today: The village of Jaba, about 9 km north-northeast of Jerusalem.
key: Geba was given to the priests as a Levitical city from Benjamin (Joshua 21).
Jonathan defeated the Philistine garrison at Geba, provoking war with the Philistines (1 Samuel 13).
King Asa built up Geba using stones Baasha had used to fortify Ramah (1 Kings 15).
Josiah defiled the high places from Geba to Beersheba (2 Kings 23).
Zechariah foresaw the land from Geba to Rimmon becoming a plain (Zechariah 14).

gezer_463.name: Gezer
gezer_463.what: A strategic Canaanite city guarding the route from the coastal plain up to Jerusalem.
gezer_463.today: Tel Gezer, between Jerusalem and Tel Aviv near Ramla.
key: Horam king of Gezer came to help Lachish, and Joshua struck him down (Joshua 10).
Ephraim did not drive out the Canaanites living in Gezer (Joshua 16).
David struck down the Philistines from Geba to Gezer (2 Samuel 5).
Pharaoh captured Gezer and gave it as a dowry to his daughter, Solomon's wife, and Solomon rebuilt it (1 Kings 9).
Sibbecai killed a descendant of the giants in a battle with the Philistines at Gezer (1 Chronicles 20).

holy_place_575.name: Holy Place
holy_place_575.what: The outer sacred room of the tabernacle and temple, in front of the Most Holy Place.
holy_place_575.today: Solomon's temple stood on the Temple Mount in Jerusalem; it no longer exists.
key: When the priests came out of the Holy Place, the cloud of the Lord's glory filled the temple (1 Kings 8).
Hezekiah ordered the Levites to carry the filth out of the Holy Place and restore worship (2 Chronicles 29).
Ezekiel's guide measured the nave of the visionary temple (Ezekiel 41).
Hebrews describes the tabernacle's first section, with the lampstand and table, as the Holy Place (Hebrews 9).

joppa_652.name: Joppa
joppa_652.what: An ancient port city on the Mediterranean coast of Israel.
joppa_652.today: Jaffa, the old port district of Tel Aviv-Yafo, Israel.
key: Hiram of Tyre floated cedar logs on rafts to Joppa for Solomon's temple (2 Chronicles 2).
Cedar for the second temple was again shipped to Joppa (Ezra 3).
Jonah went down to Joppa and boarded a ship for Tarshish to flee from the Lord (Jonah 1).
Peter raised Tabitha, also called Dorcas, from the dead in Joppa (Acts 9).
On a rooftop in Joppa, Peter received the vision preparing him to visit Cornelius (Acts 10).

rabbah_966.name: Rabbah
rabbah_966.what: The capital city of the Ammonites, east of the Jordan.
key: The iron bed of Og king of Bashan was kept in Rabbah (Deuteronomy 3).
While Joab besieged Rabbah, David sinned with Bathsheba and had Uriah killed (2 Samuel 11).
David captured Rabbah and took the crown from its king's head (2 Samuel 12).
Shobi of Rabbah brought supplies to David at Mahanaim during Absalom's revolt (2 Samuel 17).
Prophets announced that Rabbah would be destroyed in judgment (Amos 1).

issachar_1288.name: Issachar
issachar_1288.what: The tribal territory of Issachar, centered on the fertile Jezreel Valley in northern Israel.
issachar_1288.today: The eastern Jezreel Valley and lower Galilee in northern Israel.
key: Manasseh held some towns within Issachar, such as Beth-shean (Joshua 17).
Issachar received the fourth lot, including Jezreel and Shunem (Joshua 19).
Jehoshaphat son of Paruah served as Solomon's district officer in Issachar (1 Kings 4).
Issachar receives a portion in Ezekiel's vision of the restored land (Ezekiel 48).

mahanaim_756.name: Mahanaim
mahanaim_756.what: A town in Gilead east of the Jordan, near the Jabbok River.
mahanaim_756.today: Likely Tell edh-Dhahab el-Gharbi on the Jabbok River in Jordan.
key: Jacob met the angels of God here and named the place Mahanaim (Genesis 32).
It became a Levitical city in the territory of Gad (Joshua 21).
Abner made Saul's son Ish-bosheth king at Mahanaim (2 Samuel 2).
David took refuge at Mahanaim when fleeing from Absalom (2 Samuel 17).
Barzillai provided for David while he stayed at Mahanaim (2 Samuel 19).

ramah_975.name: Ramah
ramah_975.what: The hometown of Samuel's family in the hill country of Ephraim and Benjamin.
ramah_975.today: Exact site uncertain; possibly er-Ram or Nebi Samwil, just north of Jerusalem.
key: Elkanah and Hannah lived in Ramah, where Samuel was born (1 Samuel 1).
Samuel judged Israel from his home in Ramah and built an altar there (1 Samuel 7).
Israel's elders came to Samuel at Ramah and asked for a king (1 Samuel 8).
David fled from Saul to Samuel at Ramah (1 Samuel 19).
Samuel died and was buried in his house at Ramah (1 Samuel 25).

tirzah_1170.name: Tirzah
tirzah_1170.what: A Canaanite city that became the early capital of the northern kingdom of Israel.
tirzah_1170.today: Likely Tell el-Far'ah North, northeast of Nablus in the West Bank.
key: The king of Tirzah was among the kings Joshua defeated (Joshua 12).
Jeroboam's son died as his mother returned home to Tirzah (1 Kings 14).
Baasha reigned over Israel from Tirzah (1 Kings 15).
Zimri burned the palace over himself at Tirzah, and Omri later moved the capital to Samaria (1 Kings 16).
The bride in the Song is called beautiful as Tirzah (Song of Solomon 6).

ammon_58.name: Ammon
ammon_58.what: A nation east of the Jordan descended from Lot, often hostile to Israel.
ammon_58.today: The region around Amman in central Jordan.
key: God told Israel not to harass the Ammonites, since he had given their land to Lot's descendants (Deuteronomy 2).
Jephthah defeated the Ammonites after they oppressed Israel (Judges 11).
Ammon, Moab, and Mount Seir attacked Judah but destroyed one another (2 Chronicles 20).
Nehemiah enforced the law excluding Ammonites from God's assembly (Nehemiah 13).
Ezekiel announced judgment on Ammon for rejoicing over Jerusalem's fall (Ezekiel 25).

arnon_92.name: Arnon
arnon_92.what: A deep river gorge flowing into the Dead Sea, forming Moab's northern border.
arnon_92.today: Wadi Mujib in Jordan, east of the Dead Sea.
key: Israel camped beyond the Arnon, the boundary between Moab and the Amorites (Numbers 21).
Balak met Balaam at a city on the Arnon (Numbers 22).
Jephthah reminded the Ammonites that Israel had never crossed the Arnon into Moab (Judges 11).
Jeremiah announced Moab's destruction to be proclaimed by the Arnon (Jeremiah 48).

cyprus_316.name: Cyprus
cyprus_316.what: A large island in the eastern Mediterranean Sea.
key: The prophets mention Cyprus as a distant coastland trading with Tyre (Ezekiel 27).
Barnabas, a Levite native of Cyprus, sold a field and gave the money to the apostles (Acts 4).
Believers scattered after Stephen's death spread the word as far as Cyprus (Acts 11).
Barnabas and Saul preached across Cyprus, where the proconsul Sergius Paulus believed (Acts 13).
Barnabas took Mark and sailed to Cyprus after parting with Paul (Acts 15).

great_sea_493.name: Great Sea
great_sea_493.what: The Mediterranean Sea, forming the western border of the Promised Land.
key: God set the Great Sea as the western boundary of Canaan (Numbers 34).
God promised Joshua land stretching to the Great Sea toward the sunset (Joshua 1).
Kings along the coast of the Great Sea gathered to fight Israel (Joshua 9).
In Ezekiel's vision, the river from the temple makes the Dead Sea teem with fish like the Great Sea (Ezekiel 47).

jabesh-gilead_611.name: Jabesh-gilead
jabesh-gilead_611.what: A town in Gilead east of the Jordan, closely tied to King Saul.
jabesh-gilead_611.today: Possibly Tell el-Maqlub on Wadi Yabis in northern Jordan.
key: Israel struck Jabesh-gilead for not joining the assembly, and its young women were given to Benjamin (Judges 21).
Saul rescued Jabesh-gilead from Nahash the Ammonite (1 Samuel 11).
Its men recovered the bodies of Saul and his sons from Beth-shan and buried them (1 Samuel 31).
David blessed the men of Jabesh-gilead for burying Saul (2 Samuel 2).
David later moved the bones of Saul and Jonathan from Jabesh-gilead to their family tomb (2 Samuel 21).

jazer_628.name: Jazer
jazer_628.what: An Amorite town in Gilead east of the Jordan, known for its pastureland and vineyards.
jazer_628.today: Exact site uncertain; in Gilead, west of Amman, Jordan.
key: Israel captured Jazer and its villages from the Amorites (Numbers 21).
Gad and Reuben saw that the land of Jazer was good for livestock (Numbers 32).
Jazer was given to the Levites as a city in Gad (Joshua 21).
David's census officers passed through Jazer (2 Samuel 24).
Isaiah pictured Jazer weeping over the ruined vines of Moab (Isaiah 16).

megiddo_777.name: Megiddo
megiddo_777.what: A fortified city guarding a key pass into the Jezreel Valley.
megiddo_777.today: Tel Megiddo in the Jezreel Valley, northern Israel.
key: Manasseh did not drive out the Canaanites of Megiddo (Judges 1).
Deborah's song recalls the kings of Canaan fighting by the waters of Megiddo (Judges 5).
Solomon rebuilt Megiddo with forced labor (1 Kings 9).
King Ahaziah of Judah fled from Jehu and died at Megiddo (2 Kings 9).
King Josiah was killed at Megiddo by Pharaoh Neco (2 Kings 23).

most_holy_place_827.name: Most Holy Place
most_holy_place_827.what: The innermost room of the tabernacle and temple, where the ark of the covenant was kept.
most_holy_place_827.today: Solomon's temple stood on the Temple Mount in Jerusalem; it no longer exists.
key: Solomon built the inner sanctuary, overlaid it with gold, and placed two olivewood cherubim inside (1 Kings 6).
The priests brought the ark into the Most Holy Place beneath the cherubim's wings (1 Kings 8).
Aaron and his sons served the Most Holy Place and made atonement for Israel (1 Chronicles 6).
Ezekiel's guide measured the Most Holy Place of the visionary temple (Ezekiel 41).

reuben_1282.name: Reuben
reuben_1282.what: The tribal territory of Reuben on the plateau east of the Dead Sea.
reuben_1282.today: Central Jordan, north of Wadi Mujib and east of the Dead Sea.
key: Reuben and Gad asked Moses for land east of the Jordan because of their livestock (Numbers 32).
Moses gave Reuben land from Aroer on the Arnon, including Heshbon and Dibon (Joshua 13).
Reuben gave the Levites four cities, including Bezer (Joshua 21).

ziklag_1259.name: Ziklag
ziklag_1259.what: A town in the Negev given to David by the Philistine king Achish.
ziklag_1259.today: Possibly Tel Sera or Tel Halif in the northwestern Negev, Israel.
key: Ziklag was allotted to Judah and then to Simeon (Joshua 19).
Achish king of Gath gave Ziklag to David as he fled from Saul (1 Samuel 27).
Amalekites burned Ziklag, and David pursued them and recovered everything (1 Samuel 30).
At Ziklag, David received news of Saul's death (2 Samuel 1).
Mighty men came to join David at Ziklag (1 Chronicles 12).

ashkelon_103.name: Ashkelon
ashkelon_103.what: One of the five chief cities of the Philistines, on the Mediterranean coast.
ashkelon_103.today: Tel Ashkelon, within the modern city of Ashkelon, Israel.
key: Judah captured Ashkelon after Joshua's death (Judges 1).
Samson killed thirty men of Ashkelon to pay a lost wager (Judges 14).
The Philistines sent a guilt offering to Israel for Ashkelon after taking the ark (1 Samuel 6).
David lamented Saul and Jonathan, urging that the news not reach Ashkelon (2 Samuel 1).
Several prophets announced judgment on Ashkelon (Zephaniah 2).

bethany_186.name: Bethany
bethany_186.what: A village on the Mount of Olives near Jerusalem, home of Mary, Martha, and Lazarus.
bethany_186.today: Al-Eizariya, about 3 km east of Jerusalem in the West Bank.
key: Jesus stayed overnight in Bethany during his final week (Matthew 21).
A woman anointed Jesus at the home of Simon the leper in Bethany (Mark 14).
Jesus raised Lazarus from the dead in Bethany (John 11).
Mary anointed Jesus' feet at a dinner in Bethany six days before Passover (John 12).
Jesus led his disciples out as far as Bethany and was carried up into heaven (Luke 24).

goshen_490.name: Goshen
goshen_490.what: A fertile region of Egypt where Jacob's family settled.
goshen_490.today: The eastern Nile Delta of Egypt, likely around Wadi Tumilat.
key: Joseph invited his father to live in Goshen, near him (Genesis 45).
Joseph met his father Jacob in Goshen (Genesis 46).
Pharaoh granted Jacob's family the land of Goshen for their flocks (Genesis 47).
God kept the swarms of flies out of Goshen, where Israel lived (Exodus 8).
Hail struck Egypt, but not the land of Goshen (Exodus 9).

hazor_545.name: Hazor
hazor_545.what: A major Canaanite city north of the Sea of Galilee.
hazor_545.today: Tel Hazor, north of the Sea of Galilee in Israel.
key: Jabin king of Hazor led a northern coalition, and Joshua burned the city (Joshua 11).
Later, Jabin king of Canaan reigned in Hazor and oppressed Israel through Sisera (Judges 4).
Samuel recalled how God sold Israel into the hand of Sisera of Hazor (1 Samuel 12).
Solomon rebuilt Hazor with forced labor (1 Kings 9).
The Assyrian king Tiglath-pileser captured Hazor and exiled its people (2 Kings 15).

mount_of_olives_861.name: Mount of Olives
mount_of_olives_861.what: A ridge east of Jerusalem across the Kidron Valley.
mount_of_olives_861.today: The ridge facing the Old City of Jerusalem from the east.
key: David went up the Mount of Olives weeping as he fled from Absalom (2 Samuel 15).
Zechariah foresaw the Lord standing on the Mount of Olives as it splits in two (Zechariah 14).
Jesus began his entry into Jerusalem from the Mount of Olives (Matthew 21).
Seated on the Mount of Olives, Jesus taught about the end of the age (Matthew 24).
After the Last Supper, Jesus went to the Mount of Olives to pray (Luke 22).

riblah_1001.name: Riblah
riblah_1001.what: A town in Syria used as a military headquarters by Egyptian and Babylonian kings.
riblah_1001.today: Ribleh, on the Orontes River south of Homs, Syria.
key: Pharaoh Neco imprisoned King Jehoahaz of Judah at Riblah (2 Kings 23).
At Riblah, Nebuchadnezzar killed Zedekiah's sons before his eyes and blinded him (2 Kings 25).
Nebuchadnezzar also executed the nobles of Judah at Riblah (Jeremiah 39).
Judah's chief priest and officials were executed at Riblah (Jeremiah 52).

river_of_arnon_1225.name: Valley of the Arnon
river_of_arnon_1225.what: The deep gorge of the Arnon River, forming the southern border of Israel's land east of the Jordan.
river_of_arnon_1225.today: Wadi Mujib in Jordan, east of the Dead Sea.
key: God told Israel to cross the Valley of the Arnon and fight Sihon (Deuteronomy 2).
Israel took the land from the Valley of the Arnon to Mount Hermon (Deuteronomy 3).
Reuben's territory began at Aroer on the edge of the Valley of the Arnon (Joshua 13).
Hazael of Syria struck Israel's land as far as the Valley of the Arnon (2 Kings 10).

zobah_1272.name: Zobah
zobah_1272.what: An Aramean kingdom north of Damascus.
zobah_1272.today: Likely the Beqaa Valley of Lebanon and neighboring parts of Syria.
key: Saul fought against the kings of Zobah (1 Samuel 14).
David defeated Hadadezer king of Zobah near the Euphrates (2 Samuel 8).
The Ammonites hired Syrians of Zobah to fight David, but Joab routed them (2 Samuel 10).
Igal of Zobah was among David's mighty men (2 Samuel 23).
Rezon fled from Hadadezer of Zobah and became Solomon's adversary in Damascus (1 Kings 11).

achaia_16.name: Achaia
achaia_16.what: The Roman province of southern Greece, with Corinth as its capital.
achaia_16.today: Southern Greece, including Corinth and Athens.
key: Gallio, proconsul of Achaia, dismissed the Jews' charges against Paul in Corinth (Acts 18).
Paul resolved to pass through Macedonia and Achaia before going to Jerusalem (Acts 19).
Believers in Achaia gave a contribution for the poor saints in Jerusalem (Romans 15).
Stephanas' household were the first converts in Achaia (1 Corinthians 16).
The faith of the Thessalonians became an example to believers in Achaia (1 Thessalonians 1).

haran_527.name: Haran
haran_527.what: A city in upper Mesopotamia where Abraham's family settled and Laban lived.
haran_527.today: Harran, in southeastern Turkey near the Syrian border.
key: Terah settled in Haran with Abram and died there (Genesis 11).
Abram left Haran for Canaan at the Lord's call, aged seventy-five (Genesis 12).
Rebekah sent Jacob to her brother Laban in Haran to escape Esau (Genesis 27).
Jacob met Rachel by a well near Haran (Genesis 29).
Sennacherib boasted that Assyria had destroyed Haran (2 Kings 19).

kadesh-barnea_663.name: Kadesh-barnea
kadesh-barnea_663.what: An oasis on the southern edge of Canaan where Israel camped during the wilderness years.
kadesh-barnea_663.today: Likely Ein el-Qudeirat in northeastern Sinai, Egypt.
key: Moses sent the spies from Kadesh-barnea to see the land (Numbers 32).
Kadesh-barnea marked the southern boundary of the Promised Land (Numbers 34).
Israel rebelled at Kadesh-barnea, refusing to go up into the land (Deuteronomy 9).
Joshua struck down cities from Kadesh-barnea to Gaza (Joshua 10).
Caleb recalled being sent from Kadesh-barnea as a spy at age forty (Joshua 14).

lebo-hamath_723.name: Lebo-hamath
lebo-hamath_723.what: A place in the north marking the ideal northern border of Israel's land.
lebo-hamath_723.today: Possibly Lebweh in the northern Beqaa Valley of Lebanon.
key: The twelve spies explored the land as far north as Lebo-hamath (Numbers 13).
God set Lebo-hamath on the northern boundary of the land (Numbers 34).
All Israel from Lebo-hamath to the Brook of Egypt celebrated the temple's dedication (1 Kings 8).
Jeroboam II restored Israel's border from Lebo-hamath to the Sea of the Arabah (2 Kings 14).

mount_hor_842.name: Mount Hor
mount_hor_842.what: A mountain on the border of Edom where Aaron died.
mount_hor_842.today: Exact site unknown; traditionally Jebel Harun near Petra, Jordan.
key: Aaron died on Mount Hor after his garments were placed on his son Eleazar (Numbers 20).
Israel set out from Mount Hor to go around Edom (Numbers 21).
Aaron died on Mount Hor at age 123, in the fortieth year after the exodus (Numbers 33).
God told Moses he would die on Nebo as Aaron died on Mount Hor (Deuteronomy 32).

mount_seir_852.name: Mount Seir
mount_seir_852.what: The mountainous region of Edom, given to Esau's descendants.
mount_seir_852.today: The mountains of southern Jordan, east of the Arabah valley.
key: Israel traveled around Mount Seir for many days (Deuteronomy 2).
God gave Mount Seir to Esau and forbade Israel to take it (Deuteronomy 2).
Simeonites went to Mount Seir and destroyed the remaining Amalekites (1 Chronicles 4).
Men of Mount Seir joined an attack on Judah but were destroyed (2 Chronicles 20).
Ezekiel prophesied that Mount Seir would become desolate (Ezekiel 35).

ophir_911.name: Ophir
ophir_911.what: A distant land famous for its fine gold, reached by ship.
ophir_911.today: Exact site unknown; possibly southern Arabia, East Africa, or India.
key: Solomon's fleet with Hiram's sailors brought gold from Ophir (1 Kings 9).
Hiram's ships also brought almug wood and precious stones from Ophir (1 Kings 10).
Jehoshaphat's ships bound for Ophir were wrecked at Ezion-geber (1 Kings 22).
David gave gold of Ophir for building the temple (1 Chronicles 29).
Job says wisdom cannot be bought with the gold of Ophir (Job 28).

paddan-aram_916.name: Paddan-aram
paddan-aram_916.what: The region of upper Mesopotamia around Haran, home of Abraham's relatives.
paddan-aram_916.today: The area around Harran in southeastern Turkey and northern Syria.
key: Isaac married Rebekah, daughter of Bethuel the Aramean of Paddan-aram (Genesis 25).
Isaac sent Jacob to Paddan-aram to take a wife from Laban's daughters (Genesis 28).
Jacob left Paddan-aram with the livestock he had gained there (Genesis 31).
God appeared to Jacob again after he came from Paddan-aram and renamed him Israel (Genesis 35).

river_1010.name: Euphrates River
river_1010.what: The Euphrates, often called simply the River, the great river of Mesopotamia.
river_1010.today: The Euphrates River, flowing through Turkey, Syria, and Iraq.
key: Balak sent for Balaam at Pethor, near the River (Numbers 22).
God promised Israel territory reaching to the River (Deuteronomy 11).
Joshua reminded Israel that their fathers served other gods beyond the River (Joshua 24).
Isaiah warned that the Lord would use the king of Assyria from beyond the River (Isaiah 7).
Zechariah foresaw the coming king ruling from the River to the ends of the earth (Zechariah 9).

succoth_1113.name: Succoth
succoth_1113.what: A town in the Jordan Valley east of the river, near the Jabbok.
succoth_1113.today: Likely Tell Deir Alla in the Jordan Valley, Jordan.
key: Jacob built a house and shelters for his livestock and named the place Succoth (Genesis 33).
Succoth was allotted to the tribe of Gad (Joshua 13).
The officials of Succoth refused Gideon bread, and he later punished them (Judges 8).
Solomon's bronze temple furnishings were cast in clay ground between Succoth and Zarethan (1 Kings 7).

aijalon_40.name: Aijalon
aijalon_40.what: A town in the Shephelah guarding the Aijalon Valley route to Jerusalem.
aijalon_40.today: Near the village of Yalo, close to Latrun, west of Jerusalem.
key: Aijalon was allotted to Dan and given to the Levites (Joshua 21).
The Amorites persisted in living in Aijalon (Judges 1).
Israel struck the Philistines from Michmash to Aijalon (1 Samuel 14).
Rehoboam fortified Aijalon (2 Chronicles 11).
The Philistines captured Aijalon during Ahaz's reign (2 Chronicles 28).

aroer_93.name: Aroer
aroer_93.what: A town on the north rim of the Arnon gorge east of the Dead Sea.
aroer_93.today: Khirbet Ara'ir, on the northern edge of Wadi Mujib, Jordan.
key: Israel took every city from Aroer on the edge of the Arnon to Gilead (Deuteronomy 2).
Aroer marked the southern edge of Reuben's territory (Joshua 13).
Jephthah said Israel had lived in Aroer for three hundred years (Judges 11).
Hazael of Syria struck Israel as far as Aroer (2 Kings 10).
Jeremiah told the people of Aroer to watch for Moab's fleeing refugees (Jeremiah 48).

chaldea_282.name: Chaldea
chaldea_282.what: Southern Mesopotamia, the homeland of the Chaldeans who ruled Babylon.
key: Isaiah called the exiles to go out from Babylon and flee from Chaldea (Isaiah 48).
Jeremiah announced that Chaldea would be plundered (Jeremiah 50).
The Spirit brought Ezekiel in a vision to the exiles in Chaldea (Ezekiel 11).
Ezekiel rebuked Jerusalem for seeking alliances with Chaldea (Ezekiel 23).

dan_1283.name: Dan
dan_1283.what: The original tribal territory of Dan, west of Benjamin toward the Mediterranean coast.
dan_1283.today: The area between Jerusalem and Tel Aviv in central Israel.
key: Dan received the seventh lot, including Zorah, Eshtaol, and Joppa's vicinity (Joshua 19).
The Amorites pressed the Danites back into the hill country (Judges 1).
Lacking an inheritance, the Danites migrated north and seized Laish, renaming it Dan (Judges 18).

debir_325.name: Debir
debir_325.what: A Canaanite city in the hill country of Judah, southwest of Hebron.
debir_325.today: Possibly Khirbet Rabud, southwest of Hebron in the West Bank.
key: Joshua captured Debir and struck down its king (Joshua 10).
Joshua cut off the Anakim from Debir (Joshua 11).
Othniel captured Debir and received Caleb's daughter Achsah as his wife (Joshua 15).
Debir was given to the priests as a Levitical city (Joshua 21).

dibon_331.name: Dibon
dibon_331.what: A Moabite town north of the Arnon, later held by Israel.
dibon_331.today: Dhiban, in central Jordan north of Wadi Mujib.
key: Israel's victory over Sihon brought Heshbon's land as far as Dibon (Numbers 21).
The Gadites rebuilt Dibon (Numbers 32).
Moses allotted Dibon to Reuben (Joshua 13).
Isaiah pictured Dibon going up to its high places to weep (Isaiah 15).
Jeremiah announced Dibon's humiliation in Moab's judgment (Jeremiah 48).

gerar_459.name: Gerar
gerar_459.what: A town in the western Negev ruled by Abimelech in the patriarchs' time.
gerar_459.today: Likely Tel Haror, between Gaza and Beersheba in Israel.
key: The Canaanites' territory extended toward Gerar (Genesis 10).
Abraham called Sarah his sister to Abimelech king of Gerar, and God protected her (Genesis 20).
Isaac lived in Gerar during a famine and reopened wells amid disputes (Genesis 26).
Asa pursued the defeated Ethiopians as far as Gerar (2 Chronicles 14).

geshur_461.name: Geshur
geshur_461.what: A small Aramean kingdom east of the Sea of Galilee.
geshur_461.today: The Golan Heights region, east of the Sea of Galilee.
key: Israel did not drive out the Geshurites (Joshua 13).
David married Maacah, daughter of Talmai king of Geshur, the mother of Absalom (2 Samuel 3).
Absalom fled to Geshur for three years after killing Amnon (2 Samuel 13).
Joab brought Absalom back from Geshur to Jerusalem (2 Samuel 14).

hormah_580.name: Hormah
hormah_580.what: A Canaanite town in the Negev whose name recalls its devotion to destruction.
hormah_580.today: Exact site uncertain; possibly Tel Masos, east of Beersheba.
key: Israel presumed to attack without God and was beaten back as far as Hormah (Numbers 14).
Israel devoted the Canaanite cities to destruction and named the place Hormah (Numbers 21).
Judah and Simeon destroyed Zephath and called it Hormah (Judges 1).
David sent plunder from the Amalekites to Hormah (1 Samuel 30).

kedar_674.name: Kedar
kedar_674.what: An Arabian desert people and region descended from Ishmael's son Kedar.
kedar_674.today: The north Arabian desert, in modern Saudi Arabia and Jordan.
key: The psalmist laments dwelling among the tents of Kedar (Psalm 120).
The bride compares herself to the dark tents of Kedar (Song of Solomon 1).
Isaiah foresaw the flocks of Kedar gathered to Zion (Isaiah 60).
Jeremiah announced that Nebuchadnezzar would strike Kedar (Jeremiah 49).
Kedar's princes traded lambs, rams, and goats with Tyre (Ezekiel 27).

kedesh_676.name: Kedesh
kedesh_676.what: A fortified city of Naphtali in Upper Galilee and a city of refuge.
kedesh_676.today: Tel Kedesh, northwest of Lake Hula in northern Israel.
key: Kedesh was allotted to Naphtali (Joshua 19).
Kedesh in Galilee was set apart as a city of refuge (Joshua 20).
Barak came from Kedesh, and Deborah went there with him to gather troops (Judges 4).
Tiglath-pileser captured Kedesh and exiled its people to Assyria (2 Kings 15).

kidron_687.name: Kidron
kidron_687.what: The valley and seasonal stream between Jerusalem's temple hill and the Mount of Olives.
kidron_687.today: The Kidron Valley, east of Jerusalem's Old City.
key: David crossed the brook Kidron as he fled from Absalom (2 Samuel 15).
Solomon warned Shimei that crossing the Kidron would cost his life (1 Kings 2).
Asa burned his grandmother's Asherah image at the brook Kidron (1 Kings 15).
Josiah burned the idolatrous objects from the temple in the Kidron Valley (2 Kings 23).
Hezekiah's Levites carried the temple's uncleanness out to the Kidron (2 Chronicles 29).

michmash_793.name: Michmash
michmash_793.what: A town in Benjamin across a steep ravine from Geba, north of Jerusalem.
michmash_793.today: The village of Mukhmas, northeast of Jerusalem in the West Bank.
key: The Philistines encamped at Michmash with a huge army against Saul (1 Samuel 13).
Jonathan and his armor-bearer attacked the Philistine garrison at the pass of Michmash (1 Samuel 14).
Men of Benjamin resettled Michmash after the exile (Nehemiah 11).
Isaiah pictured the Assyrian army storing its baggage at Michmash (Isaiah 10).

rome_1013.name: Rome
rome_1013.what: The capital city of the Roman Empire.
key: Visitors from Rome heard the apostles at Pentecost (Acts 2).
Aquila and Priscilla had left Rome when Claudius expelled the Jews (Acts 18).
The Lord told Paul he must testify about him in Rome (Acts 23).
Paul lived in Rome under guard for two years, proclaiming the kingdom of God (Acts 28).
Paul wrote to all God's beloved in Rome, eager to preach the gospel there (Romans 1).

salt_sea_1021.name: Salt Sea
salt_sea_1021.what: The Dead Sea, the salty lake at the lowest point of the Jordan Valley.
salt_sea_1021.today: The Dead Sea, between Israel, the West Bank, and Jordan.
key: Four kings fought five kings in the Valley of Siddim, that is, the Salt Sea (Genesis 14).
The Salt Sea formed part of the eastern boundary of the land (Numbers 34).
When Israel crossed the Jordan, the waters flowing to the Salt Sea were cut off (Joshua 3).
Judah's boundary began at the southern end of the Salt Sea (Joshua 15).

zoar_1271.name: Zoar
zoar_1271.what: A small city near the southern end of the Dead Sea, spared when Sodom was destroyed.
zoar_1271.today: Likely near Safi, southeast of the Dead Sea in Jordan.
key: Lot chose the well-watered Jordan Valley stretching toward Zoar (Genesis 13).
The king of Bela, that is, Zoar, fought against the four kings (Genesis 14).
Lot fled to Zoar, which God spared, before fire fell on Sodom (Genesis 19).
From Mount Nebo, Moses viewed the land as far as Zoar (Deuteronomy 34).
Isaiah pictured Moab's fugitives fleeing to Zoar (Isaiah 15).

zorah_1275.name: Zorah
zorah_1275.what: A town in the Shephelah west of Jerusalem, the hometown of Samson's family.
zorah_1275.today: Tel Tzora, near Beit Shemesh in Israel.
key: Zorah was allotted to Dan (Joshua 19).
The angel of the Lord announced Samson's birth to Manoah's wife of Zorah (Judges 13).
Samson was buried between Zorah and Eshtaol in his father's tomb (Judges 16).
The Danites sent spies from Zorah to find new land (Judges 18).
Rehoboam fortified Zorah (2 Chronicles 11).

adullam_31.name: Adullam
adullam_31.what: A town in the Shephelah of Judah, known for a nearby cave where David hid.
adullam_31.today: Tel Adullam, in the Shephelah southwest of Bethlehem, Israel.
key: The king of Adullam was among the kings Joshua defeated (Joshua 12).
David escaped to the cave of Adullam, where about four hundred men joined him (1 Samuel 22).
Three of David's mighty men came to him at the cave of Adullam (2 Samuel 23).
Rehoboam fortified Adullam (2 Chronicles 11).
Micah foresaw Israel's glory fleeing to Adullam in judgment (Micah 1).

chebar_283.name: Chebar
chebar_283.what: A canal in Babylonia where Jewish exiles lived and Ezekiel received visions.
chebar_283.today: Exact site unknown; likely a canal near Nippur in southern Iraq.
key: Among the exiles by the Chebar canal, Ezekiel saw visions of God (Ezekiel 1).
Ezekiel came to the exiles at Tel-abib by the Chebar canal (Ezekiel 3).
Ezekiel recognized the cherubim as the creatures he saw by the Chebar canal (Ezekiel 10).
God's glory returning to the temple looked like the vision by the Chebar canal (Ezekiel 43).

cilicia_300.name: Cilicia
cilicia_300.what: A region in southeastern Asia Minor whose chief city was Tarsus, Paul's birthplace.
cilicia_300.today: The southern coastal region of Turkey around Tarsus and Adana.
key: Men from Cilicia disputed with Stephen (Acts 6).
The Jerusalem council sent its letter to Gentile believers in Syria and Cilicia (Acts 15).
Paul identified himself as a Jew from Tarsus in Cilicia (Acts 21).
Paul sailed past Cilicia on his voyage toward Rome (Acts 27).
After his conversion, Paul went into the regions of Syria and Cilicia (Galatians 1).

edrei_358.name: Edrei
edrei_358.what: A royal city of Og king of Bashan, east of the Jordan.
edrei_358.today: Daraa, in southern Syria near the Jordanian border.
key: Og king of Bashan came out to fight Israel at Edrei and was defeated (Numbers 21).
God told Moses not to fear Og, and Israel struck him down (Deuteronomy 3).
Og had reigned in Ashtaroth and Edrei (Joshua 12).
Edrei was allotted to the half-tribe of Manasseh (Joshua 13).

eglon_361.name: Eglon
eglon_361.what: A Canaanite city in the Shephelah of southern Judah.
eglon_361.today: Exact site uncertain; possibly Tell Aitun or Tel Hesi in southern Israel.
key: Debir king of Eglon joined four other Amorite kings against Gibeon (Joshua 10).
Joshua captured Eglon and devoted it to destruction (Joshua 10).
The king of Eglon is listed among the kings Joshua defeated (Joshua 12).
Eglon was allotted to Judah (Joshua 15).

egypt_259.name: Brook of Egypt
egypt_259.what: A seasonal stream marking the southwestern border of the Promised Land.
egypt_259.today: Likely Wadi el-Arish in northern Sinai, Egypt.
key: The Brook of Egypt formed the southern boundary of the land (Numbers 34).
Judah's border ended at the Brook of Egypt (Joshua 15).
All Israel from Lebo-hamath to the Brook of Egypt celebrated the temple's dedication (1 Kings 8).
Babylon took all Egypt's territory from the Brook of Egypt to the Euphrates (2 Kings 24).
Ezekiel's restored land extends to the Brook of Egypt (Ezekiel 47).

jabesh_610.name: Jabesh
jabesh_610.what: Short name for Jabesh-gilead, a town in Gilead east of the Jordan.
jabesh_610.today: Possibly Tell el-Maqlub on Wadi Yabis in northern Jordan.
key: The men of Jabesh asked for terms when Nahash besieged them, and Saul rescued them (1 Samuel 11).
The valiant men of Jabesh buried the bones of Saul and his sons (1 Samuel 31).
They fasted seven days after burying Saul under the tree in Jabesh (1 Chronicles 10).

jezreel_642.name: Jezreel
jezreel_642.what: A town in the hill country of Judah, home of David's wife Ahinoam.
jezreel_642.today: Exact site unknown; in the hill country south of Hebron.
key: Jezreel was a town in the hill country of Judah (Joshua 15).
David married Ahinoam of Jezreel (1 Samuel 25).
Ahinoam of Jezreel was among David's wives captured at Ziklag (1 Samuel 30).
Amnon, David's firstborn, was son of Ahinoam of Jezreel (2 Samuel 3).

judah-southern_1281.name: Judah
judah-southern_1281.what: The southern kingdom ruled by David's descendants from Jerusalem after Israel divided.
judah-southern_1281.today: Southern Israel and the southern West Bank, centered on Jerusalem.
key: After the kingdom divided, Rehoboam reigned over the people of Judah (1 Kings 12).
A man of God from Judah denounced Jeroboam's altar at Bethel (1 Kings 13).
Rehoboam built fortified cities for defense in Judah (2 Chronicles 11).
Syria and Israel threatened Judah, and Isaiah urged Ahaz to trust God (Isaiah 7).
Sennacherib of Assyria attacked all the fortified cities of Judah in Hezekiah's reign (2 Kings 18).

makkedah_760.name: Makkedah
makkedah_760.what: A Canaanite town in the Shephelah where five Amorite kings hid in a cave.
makkedah_760.today: Exact site uncertain; in the Shephelah lowlands of Judah.
key: Five fleeing Amorite kings hid in a cave at Makkedah and were executed (Joshua 10).
Joshua captured Makkedah and struck down its king (Joshua 10).
Makkedah was allotted to Judah (Joshua 15).

media_776.name: Media
media_776.what: The land of the Medes, northwest of Persia, later joined with Persia in one empire.
key: Cyrus' decree for rebuilding the temple was found at Ecbatana in Media (Ezra 6).
Ahasuerus feasted with the army chiefs of Persia and Media (Esther 1).
Isaiah called Elam and Media to besiege Babylon (Isaiah 21).
Daniel's vision showed a two-horned ram representing the kings of Media and Persia (Daniel 8).

memphis_779.name: Memphis
memphis_779.what: An ancient royal city of Egypt near the head of the Nile Delta.
memphis_779.today: Ruins at Mit Rahina, south of Cairo, Egypt.
key: Isaiah said the princes of Memphis were deluded (Isaiah 19).
Jeremiah addressed Judeans who had fled to Egypt and were living in Memphis (Jeremiah 44).
Jeremiah warned that Memphis would become a waste (Jeremiah 46).
Ezekiel announced that God would destroy the idols of Memphis (Ezekiel 30).
Hosea warned that Memphis would bury Israelites who fled to Egypt (Hosea 9).

paran_921.name: Paran
paran_921.what: A wilderness region between Sinai and Canaan, south of the Negev.
key: Ishmael grew up in the wilderness of Paran (Genesis 21).
Leaving Sinai, the cloud settled in the wilderness of Paran (Numbers 10).
Moses sent the twelve spies from the wilderness of Paran (Numbers 13).
After Samuel's death, David went down to the wilderness of Paran (1 Samuel 25).
Hadad the Edomite passed through Paran while fleeing to Egypt (1 Kings 11).

shinar_1084.name: Shinar
shinar_1084.what: The ancient name for the plain of southern Mesopotamia, where Babylon stood.
key: Nimrod's kingdom began with Babel and other cities in Shinar (Genesis 10).
People settled on a plain in Shinar and built the tower of Babel (Genesis 11).
Achan coveted and stole a beautiful cloak from Shinar (Joshua 7).
Nebuchadnezzar carried temple vessels to the land of Shinar (Daniel 1).
Zechariah saw wickedness carried in a basket to Shinar (Zechariah 5).

timnah_1164.name: Timnah
timnah_1164.what: A town in the Sorek Valley on the border between Judah and Philistine territory.
timnah_1164.today: Likely Tel Batash in the Sorek Valley, Israel.
key: Judah went up to Timnah to shear his sheep and met Tamar on the way (Genesis 38).
Timnah lay on Judah's northern boundary (Joshua 15).
Samson married a Philistine woman from Timnah and killed a lion nearby (Judges 14).
The Philistines captured Timnah during Ahaz's reign (2 Chronicles 28).

topheth_1176.name: Topheth
topheth_1176.what: A site in the Valley of Hinnom where children were burned as offerings.
topheth_1176.today: In the Hinnom Valley south of Jerusalem's Old City; exact spot unknown.
key: Josiah defiled Topheth so no one could sacrifice children there to Molech (2 Kings 23).
Jeremiah condemned Topheth and said it would be called the Valley of Slaughter (Jeremiah 7).
Jeremiah broke a clay flask, warning that God would make Jerusalem like Topheth (Jeremiah 19).

valley_of_rephaim_1214.name: Valley of Rephaim
valley_of_rephaim_1214.what: A broad valley southwest of Jerusalem on the border of Judah and Benjamin.
valley_of_rephaim_1214.today: Southwest of Jerusalem's Old City, in Jerusalem.
key: The valley marked part of the boundary between Judah and Benjamin (Joshua 15).
David twice defeated the Philistines who spread out in the Valley of Rephaim (2 Samuel 5).
Philistines camped there when three mighty men brought David water from Bethlehem (2 Samuel 23).
Isaiah compared Israel's judgment to gleaning ears in the Valley of Rephaim (Isaiah 17).

valley_of_the_son_of_hinnom_1226.name: Valley of the Son of Hinnom
valley_of_the_son_of_hinnom_1226.what: A valley south of Jerusalem where idolatrous child sacrifice was practiced.
valley_of_the_son_of_hinnom_1226.today: The valley along the west and south sides of Jerusalem's Old City.
key: Josiah defiled Topheth in the Valley of the Son of Hinnom (2 Kings 23).
King Ahaz burned his sons as offerings in this valley (2 Chronicles 28).
King Manasseh also burned his sons as offerings there (2 Chronicles 33).
Jeremiah said the valley would be renamed the Valley of Slaughter (Jeremiah 7).
Judah built high places of Baal in the valley to offer children to Molech (Jeremiah 32).

azekah_128.name: Azekah
azekah_128.what: A fortified town in the Shephelah overlooking the Elah Valley.
azekah_128.today: Tel Azekah, above the Elah Valley in Israel.
key: God threw down great hailstones on the fleeing Amorites as far as Azekah (Joshua 10).
The Philistines camped between Socoh and Azekah when Goliath challenged Israel (1 Samuel 17).
Rehoboam fortified Azekah (2 Chronicles 11).
Lachish and Azekah were Judah's last fortified cities resisting Babylon (Jeremiah 34).

beth-aven_191.name: Beth-aven
beth-aven_191.what: A place near Bethel and Ai; Hosea also uses the name for idolatrous Bethel.
beth-aven_191.today: Exact site unknown; near Bethel, north of Jerusalem in the West Bank.
key: Joshua sent spies to Ai, near Beth-aven, east of Bethel (Joshua 7).
The Philistines encamped at Michmash, east of Beth-aven (1 Samuel 13).
After Jonathan's attack, the battle passed beyond Beth-aven (1 Samuel 14).
Hosea warned Israel not to go up to Beth-aven to worship (Hosea 4).
Hosea said the people would mourn over the calf idol of Beth-aven (Hosea 10).

beth-horon_214.name: Beth-horon
beth-horon_214.what: Twin towns guarding a key pass from the coastal plain up to the hill country.
beth-horon_214.today: Beit Ur al-Fauqa and Beit Ur al-Tahta, northwest of Jerusalem in the West Bank.
key: Israel chased the Amorites down the descent of Beth-horon (Joshua 10).
Beth-horon lay on the boundary between Benjamin and Ephraim (Joshua 18).
Beth-horon was given to the Levites from Ephraim (Joshua 21).
A company of Philistine raiders went out toward Beth-horon (1 Samuel 13).
Dismissed Israelite troops raided Judah's cities from Samaria to Beth-horon (2 Chronicles 25).

bethsaida_231.name: Bethsaida
bethsaida_231.what: A fishing town near the north shore of the Sea of Galilee.
bethsaida_231.today: Likely et-Tell or el-Araj, near the north shore of the Sea of Galilee.
key: Philip, Andrew, and Peter were from Bethsaida (John 1).
Jesus fed the five thousand near Bethsaida (Luke 9).
Jesus healed a blind man at Bethsaida in two stages (Mark 8).
Jesus pronounced woe on Bethsaida for not repenting despite his mighty works (Matthew 11).
Greeks wishing to see Jesus approached Philip of Bethsaida (John 12).

bozrah_256.name: Bozrah
bozrah_256.what: A leading city of Edom, south of the Dead Sea.
key: Jobab of Bozrah reigned as an early king of Edom (Genesis 36).
Isaiah announced that the Lord has a sacrifice in Bozrah (Isaiah 34).
Isaiah pictured the Lord coming from Bozrah in crimsoned garments (Isaiah 63).
Jeremiah warned that Bozrah would become a horror and a waste (Jeremiah 49).
Amos announced fire on the strongholds of Bozrah (Amos 1).

eshtaol_411.name: Eshtaol
eshtaol_411.what: A town in the Shephelah near Zorah, linked with Samson.
eshtaol_411.today: Exact site uncertain; near modern Eshtaol, west of Jerusalem.
key: Eshtaol was allotted to Dan (Joshua 19).
The Spirit of the Lord began to stir Samson between Zorah and Eshtaol (Judges 13).
Samson was buried between Zorah and Eshtaol (Judges 16).
The Danites sent warriors from Zorah and Eshtaol to take new land (Judges 18).

ezion-geber_423.name: Ezion-geber
ezion-geber_423.what: A port at the northern tip of the Gulf of Aqaba, on the Red Sea.
ezion-geber_423.today: Near Eilat and Aqaba; possibly Tell el-Kheleifeh.
key: Israel camped at Ezion-geber during the wilderness journey (Numbers 33).
Israel passed by Elath and Ezion-geber, going around Edom (Deuteronomy 2).
Solomon built a fleet of ships at Ezion-geber (1 Kings 9).
Jehoshaphat's ships were wrecked at Ezion-geber, as Eliezer had prophesied (2 Chronicles 20).

hermon_564.name: Hermon
hermon_564.what: The tallest mountain in the region, marking the northern limit of Israel's conquest.
hermon_564.today: Mount Hermon, on the border of Lebanon and Syria, above the Golan Heights.
key: Israel took the land east of the Jordan as far as Mount Hermon (Deuteronomy 3).
Joshua's conquest reached Baal-gad below Mount Hermon (Joshua 11).
The psalmist remembers God from the land of Jordan and Hermon (Psalm 42).
Brothers dwelling in unity are like the dew of Hermon (Psalm 133).
The bride is called to come from the peaks of Senir and Hermon (Song of Solomon 4).
